t.2.56.1: Thus made to hear these harsh words by Rāma's mother, angry and stricken with grief, the king, distressed, fell to brooding.
t.2.56.2: As he brooded, there came back to his mind an evil deed which he had once committed long ago in ignorance, as one who shoots at a target by its sound.
t.2.56.4: I seek your favour, Kausalyā; see, I have joined my palms in supplication to you. For you are ever affectionate and free from cruelty, even toward others.
t.2.56.3: Distraught by that grief and by his grief for Rāma, the lord, the king, burning with these two sorrows, spoke to Kausalyā.
t.2.56.5: For women who reflect upon dharma, O queen, a husband, whether he be virtuous or devoid of virtue, is indeed a visible deity.
t.2.56.6: You, who are ever devoted to dharma and have seen the high and low of the world, ought not, though grieving yourself, to speak unkind words to one who is grieving deeply.
t.2.56.7: Hearing that piteous speech uttered by the distressed king, Kausalyā shed tears, as a channel pours forth fresh water.
t.2.56.8: Weeping and frightened, she joined her palms like a lotus and raised them to her head before the king, and in her agitation she spoke words whose syllables came out in haste.
t.2.56.9: Be gracious, I beg you with my head bowed; I have fallen to the ground before you. In being entreated by you I am struck down, O lord, for I ought not to be struck down by you.
t.2.56.10: For, O hero, she who must be appeased by her praiseworthy and wise husband is no true woman in either world.
t.2.56.11: I know what dharma is, O knower of dharma, and I know you to be a speaker of truth; but it was because I was stricken with grief for my son that I said whatever I said.
t.2.56.12: Grief destroys fortitude, grief destroys learning, grief destroys everything; there is no enemy equal to grief.
t.2.56.13: A blow that has fallen from an enemy's hand can be endured, but grief that has befallen one, even if very slight, cannot be endured.
t.2.56.14: Today the fifth night is counted since Rāma's going to dwell in the forest, and to me, whose joy has been struck down by grief, it seems like five years.
t.2.56.16: Even as Kausalyā was speaking these auspicious words, the sun grew dim in its rays, and the night came on.
t.2.56.15: For as I keep thinking of him, this grief grows in my heart, like the great waters of the ocean swelling with unflagging force.
t.2.56.17: Then the king, comforted by the words of Queen Kausalyā yet overwhelmed by grief, came under the sway of sleep.
